title: Claiming the muted-trumpet style before Jonah Jones
summary: He says he used the mute long before Jonah, going back to Dyer Jones and Fats, while Jonah was told to use mutes at the Embers.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: When you played the Embers, did -- Jonah had sort of established the idea of playing with a mute all of the time. Did you do that too? Or did you play open horn?
Oh, you did it before Jonah.
I think so. I've been accused of it. Before -- I told you about the mute with Fats, remember? (Waller?)
And with the show, in fact before Fats I was using the mute, you know, when I first met Dolly, and Dyer Jones, and all that business with the shows, and the carnivals, and all that stuff.
Jonah's told me that he didn't really like to use mutes, and then when he went into the Embers he had to. He got told, he was told to use mutes, and he had a-- he had trouble adjusting to it.
